hypothesis: The parent's only recurring trace-visible failure is a wasted model call at turn 1 of every 1-NOT episode (4/10 per branch, all three b1r0 branches): the model picks A(0, 0, 0), the last and least informative (0.28 bits vs 0.95) entry of A's 'still uncertain inputs' list, and the weak-query veto has to re-ask. If that list shows only rows the veto would accept, those re-asks should drop to 0 while final-table correctness stays 10/10 and mean queries stay about the same (parent 10.6).
behavior_changes: _state_text: each circuit's 'still uncertain inputs' now lists only open rows scoring at least WEAK_FRACTION (0.5) of the best open query. If rows are hidden, the line ends with '(its other open inputs are nearly predictable)'; if none qualify, it says 'none worth a query right now'.
preserved_behaviors: Joint-space candidate enumeration and the joint-entropy ranking of suggested queries are unchanged. An offline replay of the ranking gives the same query-count distribution as the parent.
The 'implied by the rules' list, the SOLVED lines, the veto on already-answered or already-implied queries, and the 'query>' tag that is missing its '<' all work as before.
The weak-query veto (once per turn, a repeat is accepted) stays as a backstop, and hidden rows remain legal queries.
The final step is unchanged: per-circuit lines, candidates listed most likely first, and the model's table snapped to the nearest consistent candidate.
verification: Ran check_b1r1_cand_pilot_labeled_b10g3r2_b1r1g0.py: 10/10 status=ok, parsed_final_guess=True, final table correct on 10/10 with 3/3 circuits right. Queries were 9,10,13,14,12,6,10,7,14,12 (mean 10.7, max 14; parent mean 10.6, max 15).

In every episode, calls = queries + 1, so there were zero re-asks (parent: 4 on b1r0g0, 7 on b1r0g1, 6 on b1r0g2). On i228 at turn 1 the model now picks the suggested B(0, 0, 1) instead of A(0, 0, 0).

Re-scored every accepted query against the parent's ranking: all are at 0.69 or more of the best open query. The new pattern is a C(0, 0, 0) pick at 0.78 at turn 2 on i209, i228 and i253. On i81 (14 queries vs the parent's 11) every pick was top-ranked at 1.00 of the best, so the difference comes from the answers it got, not from bad picks.

audit.py reports OK. Offline replay of the joint-entropy ranking over 300 sampled table triples per inventory shows no change from the parent; the worst case stays under 18 (3AND/3OR: max 15, 3AND/3OR/1NOT: 16 when always taking the top query, 17 when taking a random top-4 query, 1AND/5OR/2NOT: 16).
risks: Hiding low-value rows might make the model think those rows are fixed. This doesn't affect the final answer, because the final step shows the full candidate lists and snaps to a consistent table.
The model may now pick lower-ranked rows on circuits that are still fully listed (e.g. C(0, 0, 0) at 0.78). These cost a little information but pass the veto.

This change saves solver calls, not queries. With 3 AND / 3 OR the 6 mixed tables per circuit split 1:5 on every row, so up to 15 queries is unavoidable for this hypothesis space, and episodes on NOT inventories can still reach 16-17 of the 18 queries.
